question_text: Distinguish between photoperiod and critical photoperiod.

steps.label: Photoperiod
lines: Photoperiod is the duration of the light

steps.why: The photoperiod is simply a measured length of time, so the definition stays short; the second line prepares the contrast by pointing out that this length keeps changing.
common_mistakes: Writing that the photoperiod is the intensity of light. It is the DURATION of light.
Writing that the photoperiod is fixed. It changes with season and place.
steps.memory_tip: Photoperiod is a reading on a clock: how many hours of light today.
steps.margin_note: One sentence and one line. Keep the space for the second half.

steps.label: Critical photoperiod

lines.text: Critical photoperiod: the day length needed

lines: Critical photoperiod is the specific day
length that is essential to start a seasonal
Ex: the day length at which flowering,
steps.why: The word critical means a threshold, so the second half needs the word specific and needs a named event — without an event there is nothing for the day length to be critical FOR.
common_mistakes: Writing that the critical photoperiod is the longest day of the year. It is the length that TRIGGERS an event.
Giving no event. Flowering, breeding or migration must be named.
steps.memory_tip: Photoperiod is any day length; critical photoperiod is the ONE day length that starts something.
steps.margin_note: One sentence with the word specific, then one named event.

insider_note: The word specific is the difference between the two terms, and an answer without a named seasonal event usually loses the second mark.
